title: Handoff Fixes Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · handoff overwrite, pictures and approvals, issue #488

short.lead: This is how the design you approved ("Design approved: Handoff overwrite 1A 2A 3A") gets built: three steps under parent issue #488, all on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff. Nothing reaches main until all three are built and pass your QA. Each step is built by one helper agent in its own copy of the repo, one at a time, and I check each before the next starts. The plan is written up in docs/4-systems/usage-handoff.md, docs/4-systems/handover-pages.md and docs/4-systems/design-loop.md, and the decision is recorded in docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it does and when it counts as done.
items: plus
Step 1, #491
Every approval line registers

Built first, because every later approval depends on it. The page builder refuses a design or plan page whose copy-box reply line the design loop would reject, unless the page is for a different repo and names it in its forRepo field. The loop also accepts the stage words after the feature name, as in "Handoff overwrite design approved 1A".

Done when verify.py checks the three reply lines you sent today. "Handoff overwrite design approved 1A" moves the stage; "Handoff overwrite design 1A" and "Handoff overwrite 1A 2A" still don't, and the loop says why. A page with a bad approval field is refused, and every built page's copy line passes the loop's own check.
plus
Step 2, #490
Pictures are written into the page file

make_page.py writes each picture into the HTML as a data: address (the picture stored as text inside the page) and stops creating the separate <page>-pics folder. A page over 16 MB, the publish limit, is refused with a message naming the largest pictures.
Done when verify.py builds a page with a PNG and an SVG and finds both inside the HTML, with no pics folder. A page with pictures, published and opened in the browser, shows every picture.
plus
Step 3, #489
Each folder saves under its own name

Each folder gets a random folder id stored in its .git folder and saves to refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>/<folder id>, so no save replaces another folder's. The pickup lists every snapshot from another folder on the branch that holds files this folder lacks, each with its own restore command. Snapshots saved under the old single name are still read.
Done when verify.py proves two folders on one branch keep separate snapshots and each pickup's restore command, run as printed, brings the other's file back.
search
Then, real test
Two desktop sessions and a published page

Fresh clones of the branch, two desktop app sessions: one edits without committing, the other opens, sees the pickup, runs its restore command as printed, and gets the identical file, and the first folder's snapshot stays on GitHub. Then I write exact steps for you to follow in the cloud test and the second-account test, and update the QA page.
Nothing is needed from you until the QA page is ready.

wrapup.summary: The build plan for three fixes under issue #488: approvals first, then pictures, then a save per folder.
wrapup.changing: No code has changed yet. The plan docs and the decision are committed, and the four issues (#488 to #491) are open.
